summary.title: Oh Shit, Git!?!
summary.one_liner: Plain-English recipes for undoing common Git mistakes, such as recovering lost commits with reflog, amending commits, moving commits to another branch, and reverting or restoring files.
takeaways: Use git reflog to find the HEAD@{index} entry from before a mistake and reset back to it.
Use git commit --amend to fold a small change into the last local commit, but never amend commits already pushed to a shared branch.
Use git revert <hash> to undo an earlier commit with a new commit, or git checkout <hash> -- <file> to restore a single file from an older version.
Use git diff --staged to see changes that have already been added to the index, since plain git diff shows nothing for them.
Resetting a borked branch to origin/master with fetch, reset --hard and clean is destructive and unrecoverable, so use it only when you accept losing local work.
summary.summary: This informal guide lists common Git situations people get themselves into, such as committing to the wrong branch, amending the wrong commit, or needing to undo changes, and gives the shell commands to fix each one. Each entry pairs a short "oh shit" problem statement with a few commands and brief notes on when they are safe or risky. It is not meant as an exhaustive reference, and it also includes a final section on resetting a repo to match its remote.
